sections.h2: Where is Lawrence County, Missouri, and what communities does it hold?
sections.html:
Lawrence County covers 613 square miles of the southwest Missouri Ozarks, with Mount Vernon as the county seat. Wikipedia reports 612 square miles of land, and the Ozark Cavefish National Wildlife Refuge lies inside the county. Dade, Greene, Christian, Stone, Barry, Newton and Jasper counties border it.

The county was organized in 1845 and named for naval officer James Lawrence, remembered for the line "Don't give up the ship!" The county's own site lists these communities: Aurora, Freistatt, Halltown, Hoberg, LaRussell, Marionville, Miller, Mt. Vernon, Pierce City, Stotts City and Verona, and part of Monett also falls inside the line.

The Census Bureau counted 38,001 people in 2020 and estimated 39,401 for July 2025, a gain of 3.7% since the April 2020 base.

sections.h2: How does Lawrence County government work?
sections.html:
Lawrence County is a Class 3 county run by a three-member County Commission. Most county offices sit in Mt. Vernon: the historic courthouse at 1 E. Courthouse Square, the Justice Center at 240 N. Main St., the Law Enforcement Center at 1525 Missouri Dr. and the Health Department at 1549 Missouri Dr.

The County Clerk is Tammy Riebe, at 1 E. Courthouse Square, Suite 101, phone 417-466-2638. The county's levy page lists a Barry-Lawrence library levy, road and bridge money and several service funds, and these sit on the bill beside your school district.

Sales tax is a separate matter. The county lists a total of 6.725% for the unincorporated county, 9.225% inside Aurora, Mt. Vernon, Marionville and Verona, 9.475% for Miller, and 9.850% for Pierce City, for the third quarter of 2025.

sections.h2: What do the Census figures show for Lawrence County housing?
sections.html:
The median owner-occupied home in Lawrence County is worth $175,100 in the 2020 to 2024 Census figures, and 73.9% of homes are owner-occupied. Median household income is $61,215, and 12.6% of residents are in poverty.

  • Households: 14,602, averaging 2.60 people
  • Housing units: 16,526 in July 2025
  • Median gross rent: $800
  • Median owner cost with a mortgage: $1,216 a month
  • Building permits in 2025: 149
  • Mean commute: 25.0 minutes

About 8.3% of residents age five and older speak a language other than English at home, and 9.0% identify as Hispanic or Latino. Employer establishments numbered 689 in 2023, and total county employment was 6,385.

sections.h2: Who sets and who collects Lawrence County property tax?
sections.html:
The Assessor sets the value, and the Collector of Revenue sends the bill. Doug Bowerman is the Assessor, in the basement of the Historic Lawrence County Courthouse in Mt. Vernon, with a mailing address of P.O. Box 188, Mt. Vernon, MO 65712, and a phone number of (417) 466-2831. Office hours are 8:00 to 4:00, Monday through Friday.

Kelli McVey, first elected Collector of Revenue in 1998, runs the collector's office at 1st Floor, Lawrence County Courthouse, #1 Courthouse Square. Each month the office deposits collections with the county treasury, which then passes them to schools, libraries, ambulance and fire districts and special road districts.

The collector's office also runs the August delinquent real estate auction, issues county merchant and auctioneer licenses, and processes escrow payments that mortgage holders send for property owners.

sections.html:
The county posts its countywide levies on its website, and these seven apply to every property in the county. School, city, fire and ambulance levies come on top of them depending on where the parcel sits.

sections.h2: When are Lawrence County tax statements due, and how do I pay?
sections.html:
Statements go out in November and should arrive by the second week of the month. They are due on receipt and become delinquent after December 31, and the collector asks anyone who has no statement by Thanksgiving to call 417-466-2410.

Failing to receive a statement does not cancel the obligation or the penalty and interest that follow. A payment postmarked after December 31 comes back unprocessed unless penalty and interest are included. Look over the statement for the mailing address, vehicles and legal description before you pay.

  • In person at the courthouse, Monday through Friday, 8:00 to 3:55
  • By mail to P.O. Box 29, Mt. Vernon, MO 65712
  • Online or by phone through the collector's website
  • With cash, personal check, money order or credit card

One check can cover every statement, and partial or incorrect payments are refused. Card costs are kept by the card company, and the office is open over the noon hour.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Lawrence County assessment?
sections.html:
Contact the Assessor's office first at (417) 466-2831, then file with the county Board of Equalization by the second Monday in July. The State Tax Commission takes the next appeal, due 30 days after the date of the Board's letter.

You can appeal even before the bill is paid. The State Tax Commission says to pay the full amount to the collector by December 31, write "paid under protest" on the check, and file a statement that names your grounds and the value you believe is right.

An appeal by a corporation, LLC, trust, estate or limited partnership has to be filed by an attorney. If you bought the house recently and never saw a notice of the value, the State Tax Commission allows a direct appeal when the purchase came less than 30 days after the county mailed the statement.

sections.h2: What happens when Lawrence County property tax goes unpaid?
sections.html:
The collector holds a delinquent real estate tax auction each August, and unpaid parcels are the ones offered. The county's pages give the month only, so call 417-466-2410 for the date, the property list and what you would owe to remove a parcel before the auction.

Missouri sets tax sale procedure in Chapter 140 of the Revised Statutes. A buyer at the auction receives a certificate, and the owner has a redemption period during which the owner can pay the amount plus interest to keep the property. The collector can tell you the amount for your parcel and the timeline for a payoff.

If you sell before the auction, the title company can pay the collector from your proceeds at closing.

sections.h2: What should I do before selling a Lawrence County house with tax due?
sections.html:
Ask the Collector for a payoff figure, then ask the Assessor to confirm acreage, address and owner of record, because corrected records make a sale smoother. A wrong parcel description is easier to fix before a buyer's title company finds it.

  • Pull the statement and compare the vehicles and legal description to your records.
  • Get the payoff and keep a copy of the paid receipt.
  • Ask your title company to prorate the current year in the contract.
  • Confirm the date of the August auction if any prior year is open.

Ask the Assessor or the Collector whether any relief program applies to your parcel before closing.

faqs.q: When are Lawrence County property taxes due?
faqs.a: They are due on receipt of the November statement and become delinquent after December 31. Payments postmarked after that date come back unprocessed unless penalty and interest are included.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Lawrence County property tax?
faqs.a: Pay at the Collector of Revenue on the first floor of the Lawrence County Courthouse in Mt. Vernon, by mail to P.O. Box 29, online, or by phone. The number is 417-466-2410.

faqs.q: Who is the Lawrence County Assessor?
faqs.a: Doug Bowerman is the Assessor. The office is in the basement of the Historic Lawrence County Courthouse, and the phone is (417) 466-2831.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to appeal a Lawrence County assessment?
faqs.a: File with the Board of Equalization by the second Monday in July. A State Tax Commission appeal follows within 30 days of the Board's decision letter.

faqs.q: Does Lawrence County hold a tax sale?
faqs.a: Yes. The Collector holds a delinquent real estate tax auction each August. Call the office at 417-466-2410 for the date and the list.
